title: Policy-as-code enforcer + Residency/Retention config-drift detector and automated evidence pipeline
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Implement a policy-as-code enforcement layer and continuous configuration-drift detector focused on two compliance domains: data residency controls (region scoping of datasets/endpoints) and retention settings (automatic TTLs and archival policies). Deliver automated evidence collection and reporting so audits can show: current state, historical timeline of drift events, remediation actions, and signed evidence bundles for regulators.
acceptance_criteria: Policies expressed in a canonical repo (infra/policies/residency and infra/policies/retention) and validated by CI on PRs
Runtime enforcer returns deterministic deny/allow decisions for control-plane operations (create/update model, storage bucket policy, dataset link) with <100ms median added latency
Drift detector scans configured sources every 15 minutes and raises alerts for out-of-policy resources with classification: residency-violation | retention-violation
Automated remediation modes implemented: (1) dry-run alert, (2) auto-repair with operator approval window, (3) auto-isolate and ticket creation. Each remediation produces an evidence record
Evidence records (JSON) are archived to customer-specific secure object store and linked to audit-report UI with tamper-evident checksum and signature
End-to-end integration tests for policy CI, enforcer, detector, remediation, and evidence pipeline included in runtime-e2e suite
Dashboard panel shows live counts: violations by project, time-to-remediation, and historical drift timeline for last 90 days
technical_design: Policy language: Open Policy Agent (Rego) stored alongside docs in infra/policies. Rego chosen for expressivity and existing team familiarity
Policy lifecycle: GitOps - PR -> CI lint/rego-test -> semantic-approval by security/compliance team -> auto-merge to protected branch -> policy bundle published to control-plane artifact-store
Runtime enforcement: control-plane middleware loads policy bundles and evaluates requests at policy decision point (PDP). PDP caches compiled Rego modules and metrics emitted to telemetry

Drift detection inputs: terraform state (for infra-managed buckets), k8s resource labels, control-plane configstore, S3 object metadata, Vault/SSM retention metadata. Normalizers canonicalize representation before evaluation

Remediation engine: policy decides recommended action; remediation runner executes idempotent steps via orchestration service with preflight checks and optional human-in-loop approval using Slack/Ticket flow

Evidence pipeline: each decision/event packaged with resource snapshot, diff, policy id, evaluation trace, remediation commands, timestamp, operator who approved. Signed using KMS key and stored to evidence-bucket/customer/<YYYY-MM>/
Telemetry & alerting: rule -> Prometheus counter + Grafana dashboard; anomalies surfaced to PagerDuty for critical violations affecting production models
Scalability: detector runs sharded by customer/project; uses change-feed (S3 events, Terraform plan webhooks) to avoid full scans where possible
implementation_steps: Create canonical policy repo structure and initial Rego rules for residency (allowed regions by tenant) and retention (min/max TTLs per data class)
CI pipeline: add rego-lint, rego-unit tests, and policy validation job that runs on PRs
Build PDP middleware and integrate into control-plane request path for model/dataset create/update APIs
Implement drift-detector service that reads change feeds and falls back to scheduled scans every 15 minutes
Wire remediation runner with RBAC checks and approval flows; add Slack/Ticket connectors and commit audit events
Design evidence artifact schema and KMS signing flow; implement archival to evidence-bucket with lifecycle rules
Create Grafana dashboards and alerts; add runbook for on-call remediation steps
Add e2e tests and load tests to validate latency and false-positive rates

decisions: Adopt Open Policy Agent (Rego) as canonical policy language
Use GitOps workflow for policy changes with CI gating and audit trail
Detector will prefer change-feed/event-driven mode with scheduled scans as fallback
Evidence artifacts must be signed with KMS and retained according to tenant retention rules
Default remediation mode is 'alert + create ticket'; auto-repair requires approval for high-risk resources
risks: False positives causing unnecessary remediation or customer disruption
Performance impact on control-plane requests if PDP evaluation not optimized
Incomplete coverage: legacy customers with out-of-band infra may not emit events leading to missed drifts
Evidence storage cost and retention liabilities if not aligned with customer contracts
KMS key compromise or rotation errors could invalidate evidence signatures
mitigations: Build a dry-run mode and staged rollout using canary tenants to calibrate rules
Cache compiled Rego modules and precompute common queries to reduce eval latency
Provide an agent/connector package for legacy infra to surface metadata and events
Quota and lifecycle policies for evidence-buckets and opt-in extended retention
Use multi-region KMS with automated rotation and include key-id in evidence headers so old signatures remain verifiable
notes: Coord with PM for customer communication matrix and opt-in behavior for auto-remediation
Need to validate legal requirements per customer region; Compliance will provide matrix
Consider exposing 'policy decision trace' to customers for transparency where SLAs permit
